title: At Risk Customers counts the right customers for the chosen days
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  1. You are signed in as an Admin (the Admin role has every permission, including Reports).
  2. You are in a location (workplace) with several months of invoice history (many customers, invoices going back more than a year). At Risk needs old invoices, which cannot be back-dated by hand.
  3. Customer W: in the At Risk table (window 120 Days), a customer with Lifetime Invoices 2 or more, whose newest invoice you will make and then undo. You have written down W's Last Invoice Date.
  4. Customer X: a customer whose only invoice is more than 12 months old (Lifetime Invoices 1, so Revenue (12 Mo) is $0.00).
  5. Customer Y: a customer with 2 or more invoices, all more than 12 months old.
custom_steps:
1. On the At Risk Customers tile click the window pill and choose 120 Days. Write down the headline and count the table rows.
  2. Look for customer X in the table.
  3. Look for customer Y in the table.
  4. Read down the table and check every row: Lifetime Invoices is 2 or more, or Revenue (12 Mo) is above $0.00.
  5. Window edge: on the window pill try each of 30, 60, 90, 120 and 180 Days, and look for a customer whose Last Invoice Date is exactly that many days before today (count calendar days, e.g. Jun 9, 2026 to Oct 7, 2026 = 120 days) and one at one day fewer. If the Create Invoice step on a work order lets you choose the invoice date, you may make such invoices instead.
  6. Make a new invoice today for customer W: Work Orders > Create Work Order > W and its asset > Save; in New Line one labor line (e.g. Labor Rate EVR Travel to EVO ($100 an hour), Estimated Time 1), tick Line Approved > Save & Close; Story > Update; Complete (finish any Missing Details window); Mark Reviewed; Finance > Create Invoice (close the New Customer Payment window without paying).
  7. Click Dashboard, set the window to 120 Days and write down the headline. Look for W in the table.
  8. Click Work Orders, open the work order you just invoiced, Finance tab > the invoice's three dots > Reverse > confirm.
  9. Click Dashboard, set the window to 120 Days, write down the headline and find W's row.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The headline is a plain number (e.g. 12, no words, no dollar sign) and equals the number of rows in the table.
  • Customer X (one invoice, $0.00 revenue in the last 12 months) is not listed. Customer Y (2 or more invoices, $0.00 recent revenue) is listed.
  • Every listed customer has Lifetime Invoices of 2 or more, or Revenue (12 Mo) above $0.00.
  • Window edge: a customer whose newest invoice is exactly the chosen number of days old is listed, and one at one day fewer is not. If no such pair exists and invoice dates cannot be chosen, write "window edge not reachable by hand" in the result comment.
  • After invoicing W today, W leaves the list and the headline drops by 1 (e.g. 12 to 11).
  • After reversing that new invoice, W is back with its earlier Last Invoice Date and the headline returns to the step 1 figure: the undone invoice is ignored when deciding W's newest invoice.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; story SV-9575 (S3), story SV-9577 (S5); Dashboard v1 PRD, Confluence 788430850 v42, read 7 Oct 2026, S5 (S5-R15, S5-R7), S3 (S3-E2). Design canvas (claude.ai/artifact/Wae9DFQ8PJQBy8mbLsL5ge, captured 2026-09-28) used for on-screen labels and navigation only: boards 09_AtRisk_After (table: Customer, Last Invoice Date, Lifetime Invoices, Revenue (12 Mo)), 09_AtRisk_Window.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S5-R15: “Two parts of the at-risk definition are fixed here so the count cannot be read two ways. "Some revenue in the last twelve months" means revenue greater than $0.00 over the trailing twelve months, measured the way the Revenue tile measures revenue: invoice subtotals before any discount and before tax, minus credit memos. A customer whose twelve-month revenue is exactly $0.00, or is negative because credits exceeded sales, does not satisfy this part of the test, though they can still qualify on the two-or-more-lifetime-invoices part. "At least the selected number of days old" is counted in whole calendar days in the selected workplace's timezone, from the date of the customer's most recent invoice to the current date. The count therefore changes at the shop's own midnight and is stable through the shop's working day, and two people viewing the same workplace from different places see the same number.”
  • S5-R7: “The At Risk Customers tile headline is the count of at-risk customers for the selected inactivity window, shown as a plain number.”
  • S3-E2: “A voided invoice is excluded from every figure the dashboard shows. It contributes nothing to Revenue or to the parts-versus-labor split, nothing to invoiced hours or invoiced technician hours, and it is counted in neither the Sales by Customer count nor the At Risk Customers count, including when deciding a customer's most recent invoice. This is not a dashboard rule of its own: it is what the reports do, and the dashboard matches them (S3-R1). A void means the document was undone, so a figure that still carried its money or its hours would overstate the shop.”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.
